newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Parliament mad cow inquiry to visit Britain.
newsitem.headline: Parliament mad cow inquiry to visit Britain.

text.p: A European Parliament team will fly to Britain on Wednesday for a three-day visit to investigate British efforts to eradicate mad cow disease, the head of a parliamentary committee of inquiry said on Tuesday.
"A small delegation will visit Britain from December 4-6," Reimer Boege, the German chairman of the inquiry into the fatal cattle brain disease, told a hearing.
The Euro MPs will meet British farmers' leaders, meat processors, consumer groups, scientists, farm ministry officials and members of parliament.
The MPs, who started the inquiry in September, have twice unsuccessfully tried to invite British Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg to give evidence.

"We feel that it is important that we are open to the British people, including British farmers and British members of the House of Commons, to tell us whatever they feel on the issue," Spanish socialist Manuel Medina said in a statement.
Medina, author of the inquiry's report which is due in February, said that the inquiry wanted to see what is going on in British slaughter houses and research laboratories.
Britain's Chief Veterinary Officer Keith Meldrum said the visit would help clear up some serious misunderstandings.
"The visit...should help clarify the controls and how they are enforced," he said in a statement to the inquiry on Tuesday.
